A kernel-based root solution for Android

A fresh boot gives the exploit a cleaner window: it runs against a settled kernel rather than the one this attempt has already been through. Restarting the phone and retrying is the better odds - the install then runs on its own after the boot, or the next time you open this app if the phone has no cached payload to run it with. Retrying straight away is faster and less likely to work.
This app could not reboot the phone - that needs root, which this run did not get - so restart it yourself. The install will start on its own when the phone is back up.

The ceilings this app puts on a run
How long one run may take before the app gives up on it. A fresh-session profile is never cut below the app\'s own hour, because those hand their pacing to the payload.
No output before the payload is stalled

How long the payload may print nothing before the app treats it as stalled and stops the run. The root helper prints nothing on purpose while a scheduler-sensitive payload is alive, so a short limit can end a healthy run: the default is the same as the whole-run ceiling, where it can never fire first. Not applied to a fresh-session profile at all.
Run limits are back to their defaults
How long a single helper command may run. Internal, and rarely the reason a run stops.

How the exploit is attempted - how many tries, how long each gets, which way it looks for the slide - is decided by the payload profile in the feed and handed over as the variables on the run plan. Those are not settings here: they belong to the payload that does the work.

Restart the Android runtime now? Everything that is open will close, and the screen will go back to the lock screen.
Let KernelSU restart the userspace now? Everything that is open will close, and the modules are walked through their normal order.
Turn root on boot off and restart the phone? Root is loaded per boot, so it will be gone when the phone comes back and you will have to root it again.
Re-apply the KernelSU module lifecycle now? Stage scripts, system.prop and the module mounts are run again. Nothing that is open is closed.
Run KernelSU\'s own module lifecycle again through the installed daemon, without restarting anything: for a module whose mounts are in place but whose stage scripts have not run
Module lifecycle re-applied. Nothing was restarted.
Recreate the Android runtime so mounted modules load their framework hooks; running apps are closed
Let KernelSU stop and restart the userspace, which walks the module lifecycle in its normal order

KernelSU is running, but this app has no root shell of its own yet. Grant Root My Galaxy superuser in the KernelSU app, or start Shizuku, and try again.
Shizuku is running, but this needs root and a Shizuku shell is not root. Restarting the userspace has to happen from a boot with KernelSU loaded: turn root on boot on, or run the install again.
